content: 1. Crampin AC et al. investigated whether recurrent tuberculosis (TB) in a general population cohort in Malawi was due to relapse or reinfection, with a focus on the impact of HIV. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2010 (Volume 24, Pages 417–426). 2. Marx FM et al. conducted a retrospective cohort study to determine the rate of sputum smear-positive TB following treatment default in high-burden settings. 3. Getahun H et al. reviewed evidence on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of TB in children and mothers, emphasizing its implications for maternal, neonatal, and child health services. This work was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2012 (Volume 205, Supplement, Pages S216–S227). 4. Figueroa-Damian R and Arredondo-Garcia JL examined neonatal outcomes in children born to women with TB, with their findings published in the Archives of Medical Research in 2001 (Volume 32, Pages 66–69). 5. Jana N et al. studied perinatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by pulmonary TB, with results published in the International Journal of Gynaecology and Obstetrics in 1994 (Volume 44, Pages 119–124). 6. Asuquo J et al. conducted a case-control study to assess the risk of adverse perinatal outcomes associated with TB during pregnancy. Their findings were published in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2012 (Volume 32, Pages 635–638). 7. Jana N et al. also explored obstetrical outcomes among women with extrapulmonary TB, with their study published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 1999 (Volume 341, Pages 645–649). 8. Kothari A, Mahadevan N, and Girling J investigated TB and pregnancy outcomes in a high-prevalence area in London, with their findings published in the European Journal of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Biology in 2006 (Volume 126, Pages 48–55). 9. Heywood S et al. conducted a survey of pregnant women with TB at the Port Moresby General Hospital, with results published in the Papua and New Guinea Medical Journal in 1999 (Volume 42, Pages 63–70). 10. Bjerkedal T, Bahna SL, and Lehmann EH studied the course and outcomes of pregnancy in women with pulmonary TB, with their findings published in the Scandinavian Journal of Respiratory Diseases in 1975 (Volume 56, Pages 245–250). 11. Nhan-Chang CL and Jones TB reviewed TB in pregnancy, with their work published in Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2010 (Volume 53, Pages 311–321). 12. Dara M et al. provided an overview of the history and evolution of immigration medical screening for TB, with their findings published in the Expert Review of Anti-infective Therapy in 2013 (Volume 11, Pages 137–146). 13. Cuevas LE et al. evaluated the use of LED fluorescence microscopy for diagnosing pulmonary TB through a multi-country cross-sectional study.
